ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: status corrected from the worker's original 'ok' to 'partial' before merge, for consistency with this project's established convention (S.N. 86 QVC, S.N. 97 H&M Home UK, S.N. 118 Connox all used 'partial' when a similarly large fraction of qty came back null+flagged, regardless of how well-justified each individual null decision was) -- 98 of 107 leaf rows here are null+MANUAL REVIEW (91%), which is a Partial-tier outcome by that precedent even though the category structure itself is fully and reliably extracted. ACCESS: robots.txt (fetched fresh via r.jina.ai/https://www.noon.com/robots.txt, HTTP 200) has NO Claude-specific block -- 'User-agent: ClaudeBot' group explicitly 'Allow: /' (also GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot all explicitly allowed), separate from and less restrictive than the generic 'User-agent: *' group which disallows only /_svc/ and /_vs/ internal service paths. This is the opposite pattern to sibling S.N. 189 Amazon UAE (which names ClaudeBot with a full-site Disallow) -- Noon UAE is clear to extract. Direct fetch of noon.com and its raw category-listing HTML returns only an empty SPA shell (no SSR product/count data, confirmed on 3 saved raw HTML pulls from the prior session) so all extraction was done via r.jina.ai (rendered DOM text), which does return full category nav, filters, product tiles and the results-count widget.

SCOPE: Per brief instruction, strictly scoped to the 'Home Decor' department subtree (home-and-kitchen/home-decor/*) taken from noon's own category-tree API dump (saved as category_tree.json, 25 top-level children under home-decor), NOT the whole 'Home & Kitchen' mega-department -- sibling departments also under Home & Kitchen but outside Home Decor (Kitchen & Dining/tableware, Patio Lawn & Garden, Bath, Storage & Organisation, Bedding, Furniture) were deliberately excluded to avoid enumerating the whole marketplace, matching the brief's explicit Target Home / Bed Bath & Beyond discipline note for this company. Within Home Decor, excluded per project rules: Home Fragrance (17 sub-nodes, all fragrance/incense/diffusers/scented candles), Artificial Flora (8 nodes incl. Christmas Trees), Slipcovers/Cushion Covers/rugs/curtains/blinds/valances/jabots (textiles), Doorstops, Draft Stoppers, Memo Boards, Umbrella Racks, Magazine Holders (functional/organisational, not decor), Photo Albums (6 nodes, paper-craft storage), Gift Baskets, Key Chain Frames, Shirt Frames, Wallpaper, Decorative Pillows (bedding-16171/decorative-pillows-16073 -- textile despite the name), Wreaths/Wreath Hangers/Tree Skirts/Cardboard Cutouts (Holiday & Gift), Tassels (textile trim), Prayer Beads/Prayer Mats (personal/textile religious items), and the duplicate 'spiritual-azaan-clocks' node (same product set as clocks-16151/azaan-clocks, Rule 0.6 facet re-cut). Light Bulbs (home-decor-lighting/home-decor-bulbs) dropped per bulb exclusion. Added beyond the prior session's plan: Fridge Magnets, Mezuzahs (decorative religious plaque, parallel to the included Quran Boxes & Holders), and Tapestries (treated as wall art/wall decor, not textile, consistent with Canvas & Framed Paintings being in scope). Rule 0.6 overlap: 'Kids Room Decor' is a room-based cross-cut with its own Lighting/Wall Decor/Mirrors nodes (kids-room-decor/lamps-and-lighting, wall-decor-24861, mirrors-17909) that are distinct URLs/product sets from the type-based Lighting and Wall Decor & Mirrors branches -- emitted separately as its own top-level group, not deduplicated, per Rule 0.6 (only exact same-listing-under-second-URL gets dropped). Kids Room Decor also has a Rugs and Kids' Curtains node -- excluded as textiles/floor coverings, consistent with the rest of the extraction. All Mirrors (Rule 0.3) and every Decor Lighting fixture type incl. outdoor lighting (Rule 0.2) traversed.

QTY VERIFICATION (Rule 1): fetched each of the 107 leaf category pages once via r.jina.ai and located the site's own 'X Results' / Arabic 'X Search Results' count widget (confirmed to be a genuine per-category/per-filter count, not a generic sitewide search placeholder -- verified by applying a brand filter to Dream Catchers, which dropped the count from '8K+' to an exact '4 Results', and by confirming the widget sits next to a removable category-name filter chip on every page). CRITICAL FINDING confirming the brief's warning: noon.com/UAE displays an EXACT integer only when the true count is under ~100 (2 leaves qualified: Mezuzahs=24, Wall-hanging Fountains=42); from 100 upward it rounds DOWN to the nearest hundred with a '+' suffix (e.g. true count 379 displays as '300+' -- confirmed by exhaustion pagination, see below), and above roughly 1000 it rounds to the nearest thousand with a 'K+' suffix (e.g. '8K+', '100K+'). A rounded '+' figure is explicitly NOT the exact number the site reports, so per 'THE ONE RULE THAT MATTERS' these were left qty:null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag rather than padding/estimating. For the 7 leaves in the cheaply-verifiable 100-999 'N00+' band, exact totals were recovered by exhaustion pagination (?page=N&limit=50, counting unique product tile IDs to the page where tiles < 50): Mantel Clocks 379 (displayed '300+'), Floor & Grandfather Clocks 203 ('200+'), Candle Sets 811 ('800+'), Floor Standing Fountains 185 ('100+'), Quran Boxes & Holders 758 ('700+'), Kids Decor Parts & Accessories 554 ('500+'), Ceiling Lights 648 ('600+'). This confirms the rounding is floor-to-hundred, not a nonsense number, and that this marketplace's true per-category inventory (many small/duplicate third-party-seller listings) genuinely runs into the thousands-to-tens-of-thousands for most single decor sub-categories -- e.g. 'Wall Pediments' shows 2K+, 'Sculptures' shows 100K+. Exhaustive pagination to an exact figure for a 1K+-100K+ category would require 20-2000+ sequential page fetches each; r.jina.ai began returning HTTP 429 after ~13-17 requests even at concurrency 3 with 8-48s backoff, so this was infeasible within budget for the remaining 98 leaves -- all 98 are left qty:null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag quoting the site's own rounded figure as evidence, which is the correct/honest answer per the brief rather than reporting an inflated or estimated number. 9 of 107 leaves carry a verified exact qty (2 direct-exact + 7 exhaustion-verified); the other 98 are flagged. No leaf fetch failed outright (107/107 pages loaded). status='ok' because the category structure itself was fully and reliably extracted and every qty decision (exact, exhaustion-verified, or null+flag) reflects a real site-reported figure or an honest inability to obtain one -- none were estimated or padded.

DUPLICATE-COMPANY CHECK: not on the brief's flagged-duplicate list; no other UAE/global Noon extraction exists yet in this project (S.N. 189 Amazon UAE, the other flagged marketplace, was stopped before extraction by its own robots.txt Claude-block, so no cross-reference applies).
